sentences.zh: 冬十一月，蜀賊譙縱陷巴東，守將溫祚、時延祖死之。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, the Shu bandit Qiao Zong took Badong; the garrison commanders Wen Zuo and Shi Yanzu died in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the Shu rebel Qiao Zong seized Badong; Wen Zuo and Shi Yanzu, the defenders, were killed.

sentences.zh: 十二月壬辰，劉裕破盧循于豫章。

translations.literal: On renchen of the twelfth month, Liu Yu defeated Lu Xun at Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen in the twelfth month Liu Yu crushed Lu Xun at Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 七年春二月壬午，右將軍劉籓斬徐道覆于始興，傳首京師。

translations.literal: On renwu of the second month of spring in the seventh year, General of the Right Liu Fan beheaded Xu Daofu at Shixing and sent the head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu in the second month of Yixi 7 Liu Fan, general of the right, executed Xu Daofu at Shixing and forwarded his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，盧循走交州，刺史杜慧度斬之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Lu Xun fled to Jiaozhou, and the inspector Du Huidu beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Lu Xun bolted to Jiaozhou, where Du Huidu, the inspector, cut him down.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丁卯，以荊州刺史劉道規爲征西大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On dingmao of autumn, the seventh month, the inspector of Jingzhou, Liu Daogui, was made Grand General Who Conquers the West, with equal ceremonial to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao in the seventh month Liu Daogui, inspector of Jingzhou, was promoted to grand general who conquers the west with three-excellency honors.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，沮渠蒙遜伐涼，涼武昭王玄盛與戰，敗之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Juqu Mengxun campaigned against Liang; Li Xuansheng, the Martial and Luminous Prince of Liang, fought him and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Juqu Mengxun invaded Western Liang; Li Gao, styled Xuansheng, met him in battle and won.

sentences.zh: 八年春二月丙子，以吳興太守孔靖爲尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: On bingzi of the second month of spring in the eighth year, the prefect of Wuxing, Kong Jing, was made Vice Director of the Right of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi in the second month of Yixi 8 Kong Jing, prefect of Wuxing, became right vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三月甲寅，山陰地陷四尺，有聲如雷。

translations.literal: On jiayin of the third month, the ground at Shanyin sank four chi, with a sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin in the third month the earth at Shanyin dropped four feet amid a noise like thunder.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，乞伏公府弑乞伏乾歸，乾歸子熾盤誅公府，僭卽偽位。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, Qifu Gongfu murdered Qifu Gan'gui; Gan'gui's son Chipan executed Gongfu and usurped the false position.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Qifu Gongfu assassinated Qifu Gan'gui; Qifu Chipan, his son, killed Gongfu and seized the usurped throne.

sentences.zh: 六月，以平北將軍魯宗之爲鎮北將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, General Who Pacifies the North Lu Zongzhi was made General Who Guards the North.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Lu Zongzhi, general who pacifies the north, was promoted to general who guards the north.

sentences.zh: 秋七月甲午，武陵王季度薨。

translations.literal: On jiawu of autumn, the seventh month, Prince Jidu of Wuling died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu in the seventh month Sima Jidu, Prince of Wuling, died.

sentences.zh: 庚子，征西大將軍劉道規卒。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Grand General Who Conquers the West Liu Daogui died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Liu Daogui, grand general who conquers the west, died.

sentences.zh: 八月，皇后王氏崩。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Empress Wang died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Empress Wang passed away.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，高密王純之薨。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Prince Chunzhi of Gaomi died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Sima Chunzhi, Prince of Gaomi, died.

sentences.zh: 九月癸酉，葬僖皇后于休平陵。

translations.literal: On guiyou of the ninth month, Empress Xi was buried at Xiuping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou in the ninth month Empress Xi was interred at Xiuping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 己卯，太尉劉裕害右將軍兗州刺史劉籓、尚書左僕射謝混。

translations.literal: On jimao, Grand Commandant Liu Yu murdered General of the Right, inspector of Yanzhou, Liu Fan, and Vice Director of the Left Xie Hun.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Liu Yu, grand commandant, had Liu Fan, general of the right and inspector of Yanzhou, and Xie Hun, left vice director of the secretariat, put to death.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，裕矯詔曰：「劉毅苞藏禍心，構逆南夏，籓、混助亂，志肆姦宄。

translations.literal: On gengchen, Yu forged an edict saying: "Liu Yi harbored a treacherous heart, raised rebellion in the southern summer, and Fan and Hun abetted the turmoil, their wills bent on villainy.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Liu Yu forged a rescript declaring that Liu Yi had nursed treason and rebelled in the south, while Liu Fan and Xie Hun abetted him in open wickedness.

sentences.zh: 賴寧輔玄鑒，撫機挫銳，凶黨卽戮，社稷乂安。

translations.literal: Thanks to the subtle insight of the guardian ministers, who seized the moment and broke their edge, the wicked faction was at once executed and the altars of soil and grain were again secure."
translations.idiomatic: Through the keen judgment of the ministers at court, who grasped the crisis and blunted the conspiracy, the traitors were cut down at once and the dynasty restored to peace."

sentences.zh: 夫好生之德，所因者本，肆眚覃仁，實資玄澤。

translations.literal: The virtue that loves life takes root in its sources; extending pardon and spreading kindness truly depends on the dark, silent power of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The mercy that cherishes life grows from its deepest source; to widen amnesty and shower grace rests on Heaven's hidden favor."

sentences.zh: 況事興大憝，禍自元凶。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the deed arose from the arch-villain, the calamity sprang from the chief culprit.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since the plot stemmed from the arch-traitor himself, guilt lies with the ringleader alone."

sentences.zh: 其大赦天下，唯劉毅不在其例。

translations.literal: Let there be a great amnesty for all under Heaven; only Liu Yi is excluded from the ordinance."
translations.idiomatic: Let a great amnesty sweep the realm—Liu Yi alone stands outside its mercy."

sentences.zh: 普增文武位一等。

translations.literal: Let civil and military ranks each be advanced one grade."
translations.idiomatic: All civil and military officials shall rise one rank."

sentences.zh: 孝順忠義，隱滯遺逸，必令聞達。

translations.literal: The filial, obedient, loyal, and righteous, and those hidden or overlooked, must be brought to the court's hearing."
translations.idiomatic: Men noted for filial piety, loyalty, or righteousness, and talent long overlooked, must be recommended until the throne knows their names."

sentences.zh: 」己丑，劉裕帥師討毅。

translations.literal: On jichou, Liu Yu led an army to campaign against Yi.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou Liu Yu took the field against Liu Yi.

sentences.zh: 裕參軍王鎮惡陷江陵城，毅自殺。

translations.literal: Yu's staff officer Wang Zhen'e took Jiangling city, and Yi killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen'e, an officer on Liu Yu's staff, stormed Jiangling; Liu Yi committed suicide.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，沮渠蒙遜僭號河西王。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, Juqu Mengxun usurped the title King of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Juqu Mengxun proclaimed himself king of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以西陵太守朱齡石爲建威將軍、益州刺史，帥師伐蜀。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the prefect of Xiling, Zhu Lingshi, was made General Who Establishes Might and inspector of Yizhou and led an army to campaign against Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Zhu Lingshi, prefect of Xiling, became general who establishes might and inspector of Yizhou and marched on Shu.

sentences.zh: 分荊州十郡置湘州。

translations.literal: Ten commanderies of Jingzhou were split off to establish Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court carved ten commanderies from Jingzhou to create a new Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 是歲，廬陵、南康地四震。

translations.literal: That year, the earth shook four times in Luling and Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: That year Luling and Nankang each felt four tremors.

sentences.zh: 九年春三月丙寅，劉裕害前將軍諸葛長民及其弟輔國大將軍黎民、從弟寧朔將軍秀之。

translations.literal: On bingyin of the third month of spring in the ninth year, Liu Yu murdered former general Zhuge Changmin and his younger brother, Grand General Who Supports the State Limin, and his cousin, General Who Calms the Northern Frontier Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin in the third month of Yixi 9 Liu Yu executed Zhuge Changmin, former general, his brother Zhuge Limin, grand general who supports the state, and his cousin Zhuge Xiuzhi, general who calms the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，加劉裕鎮西將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Liu Yu was additionally made General Who Garrisons the West and inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Liu Yu added the titles general who garrisons the west and inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 林邑范胡達寇九真，交州刺史杜慧度斬之。

translations.literal: Fan Huda of Linyi raided Jiuzhen; the inspector of Jiaozhou, Du Huidu, beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Huda of Linyi struck Jiuzhen; Du Huidu, inspector of Jiaozhou, slew him.

sentences.zh: 夏四月壬戌，罷臨沂、湖熟皇后脂澤田四十頃，以賜貧人，弛湖池之禁。

translations.literal: On renxu of summer, the fourth month, the forty qing of cosmetic-revenue fields at Linyi and Hushu belonging to the empress were abolished and given to the poor, and the prohibition on lakes and ponds was relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu in the fourth month the court surrendered forty qing of the empress's cosmetic estates at Linyi and Hushu to the needy and lifted restrictions on fishing the palace waters.

sentences.zh: 封鎮北將軍魯宗之爲南陽郡公。

translations.literal: General Who Guards the North Lu Zongzhi was enfeoffed as Duke of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zongzhi, general who guards the north, was invested duke of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，朱齡石克成都，斬譙縱，益州平。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Zhu Lingshi took Chengdu, beheaded Qiao Zong, and Yizhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Zhu Lingshi seized Chengdu, executed Qiao Zong, and brought Yizhou to peace.

sentences.zh: 九月，封劉裕次子義真爲桂陽公。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Liu Yu's second son Yizhen was enfeoffed as Duke of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Liu Yizhen, Liu Yu's second son, became duke of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月，安平王球之薨。

translations.literal: In winter, the twelfth month, Prince Qiuzhi of Anping died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Sima Qiuzhi, Prince of Anping, died.

sentences.zh: 是歲，高句麗、倭國及西南夷銅頭大師並獻方物。

translations.literal: That year, Koguryŏ, Wa, and the southwestern Yi chief Tongtou Dashī all presented local tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That year envoys arrived from Koguryŏ, from Wa, and from the southwestern tribes led by the chieftain Tongtou Dashī, each bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 十年春三月戊寅，地震。

translations.literal: On wuyin of the third month of spring in the tenth year, there was an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin in the third month of Yixi 10 the earth shook.

sentences.zh: 夏六月，乞伏熾盤帥師伐禿髮傉檀，滅之。

translations.literal: In summer, the sixth month, Qifu Chipan led an army to campaign against Tufa Rutan and destroyed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Qifu Chipan marched on Tufa Rutan and extinguished his state.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，淮北大風，壞廬舍。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, a great wind blew north of the Huai, destroying houses.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month a gale north of the Huai tore through dwellings.

sentences.zh: 九月丁巳朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: On dingsi, the first day of the ninth month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: New moon on dingsi in the ninth month: the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 林邑遣使來獻方物。

translations.literal: Linyi sent envoys to present local tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Linyi sent envoys with gifts of tribute.

sentences.zh: 是歲，城東府。

translations.literal: That year, the Eastern Offices compound was walled.
translations.idiomatic: That year work began on fortifying the Eastern Offices residence.

sentences.zh: 十一年春正月，荊州刺史司馬休之、雍州刺史魯宗之並舉兵貳於劉裕，裕帥師討之。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the eleventh year, the inspector of Jingzhou, Sima Xiuzhi, and the inspector of Yongzhou, Lu Zongzhi, both raised troops in defiance of Liu Yu; Yu led an army to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Yixi 11 Sima Xiuzhi of Jingzhou and Lu Zongzhi of Yongzhou rose against Liu Yu, who took the field to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 庚午，大赦。

translations.literal: On gengwu, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu the court declared a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，以吏部尚書謝裕爲尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Minister of Personnel Xie Yu was made Vice Director of the Left of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Xie Yu, minister of personnel, became left vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二月丁未，姚興死，子泓嗣偽位。

translations.literal: On dingwei of the second month, Yao Xing died, and his son Hong inherited the false position.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei in the second month Yao Xing died; his son Yao Hong succeeded to his usurped throne.

sentences.zh: 三月辛巳，淮陵王蘊薨。

translations.literal: On xinsi of the third month, Prince Yun of Huailing died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi in the third month Sima Yun, Prince of Huailing, died.

sentences.zh: 壬午，劉裕及休之戰于江津，休之敗，奔襄陽。

translations.literal: On renwu, Liu Yu fought Xiuzhi at the Yangzi ford; Xiuzhi was defeated and fled to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Liu Yu engaged Sima Xiuzhi at the river crossing; Xiuzhi lost and bolted to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 夏四月乙卯，青、冀二州刺史劉敬宣爲其參軍司馬道賜所害。

translations.literal: On yimao of summer, the fourth month, Liu Jingxuan, inspector of Qing and Ji provinces, was murdered by his army aide Sima Daoci.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao in the fourth month Liu Jingxuan, joint inspector of Qing and Ji, was assassinated by his staff officer Sima Daoci.

sentences.zh: 五月甲申，彗星二見。

translations.literal: On jiashen of the fifth month, two comets appeared.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen in the fifth month two comets were sighted.

sentences.zh: 甲午，休之、宗之出奔于姚泓。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Xiuzhi and Zongzhi fled in exile to Yao Hong.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Sima Xiuzhi and Lu Zongzhi crossed the border to take refuge with Yao Hong.

sentences.zh: 論平蜀功，封劉裕子義隆彭城公，朱齡石豐城公。

translations.literal: In reckoning merit for pacifying Shu, Liu Yu's son Yilong was enfeoffed as Duke of Pengcheng, and Zhu Lingshi as Duke of Fengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: For the Shu campaign Liu Yilong, Liu Yu's son, received the duchy of Pengcheng and Zhu Lingshi that of Fengcheng.

sentences.zh: 己酉，霍山崩，出銅鐘六枚。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Mount Huo collapsed, and six bronze bells emerged.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Mount Huo gave way, disgorging six bronze bells.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丙戌，京師大水，壞太廟。

translations.literal: On bingxu of autumn, the seventh month, the capital suffered great flooding, which damaged the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu in the seventh month a flood struck the capital and harmed the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 辛亥晦，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: On xinhai, the last day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, month's end, an eclipse of the sun occurred.

sentences.zh: 八月丁未，尚書左僕射謝裕卒，以尚書右僕射劉穆之爲尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: On dingwei of the eighth month, Vice Director of the Left Xie Yu died, and Vice Director of the Right Liu Muzhi was made Vice Director of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei in the eighth month Xie Yu, left vice director of the secretariat, died; Liu Muzhi, right vice director, succeeded him on the left.

sentences.zh: 九月己亥，大赦。

translations.literal: On jihai of the ninth month, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai in the ninth month the court ordered a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 十二年春正月，姚泓使其將魯軌寇襄陽，雍州刺史趙倫之擊走之。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the twelfth year, Yao Hong sent his general Lu Gui to raid Xiangyang; Zhao Lunzhi, inspector of Yongzhou, attacked and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Yixi 12 Yao Hong dispatched Lu Gui against Xiangyang, but Zhao Lunzhi, inspector of Yongzhou, repulsed him.

sentences.zh: 二月，加劉裕中外大都督。

translations.literal: In the second month, Liu Yu was additionally made supreme grand commander inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Liu Yu received the added title supreme commander for all forces at court and in the field.

sentences.zh: 夏六月，赫連勃勃攻姚泓秦州，陷之。

translations.literal: In summer, the sixth month, Helian Bobo attacked Yao Hong's Qinzhou and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Helian Bobo stormed Qinzhou for Later Qin and seized it.

sentences.zh: 己酉，新除尚書令、都鄉亭侯劉柳卒。

translations.literal: On jiyou, the newly appointed Director of the Secretariat, village marquis Liu Liu, died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Liu Liu, newly named director of the secretariat and Marquis of Duxiang village, died.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，劉裕及琅邪王德文帥衆伐姚泓。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, Liu Yu and the Prince of Langye, Dewen, led a host to campaign against Yao Hong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Liu Yu and Sima Dewen, Prince of Langye, marched against Yao Hong.

sentences.zh: 丙午，大赦。

translations.literal: On bingwu, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu a general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丙寅，姚泓將姚光以洛陽降。

translations.literal: On bingyin of winter, the tenth month, Yao Hong's general Yao Guang surrendered Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin in the tenth month Yao Guang, a general of Yao Hong, capitulated with Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 己丑，遣兼司空、高密王恢之修謁五陵。

translations.literal: On jichou, Concurrent Minister of Works, Prince Huizhi of Gaomi, was sent to perform rites at the five imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou Sima Huizhi, Prince of Gaomi, holding concurrent minister of works, was dispatched to sweep and sacrifice at the five mausolea.

sentences.zh: 十三年春正月甲戌朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, the first day of the first month of spring in the thirteenth year, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: New moon on jiaxu in the first month of Yixi 13: the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 二月，涼武昭王李玄盛薨，世子士業嗣位爲涼州牧、涼公。

translations.literal: In the second month, Li Xuansheng, the Martial and Luminous Prince of Liang, died, and his heir Shiye succeeded as shepherd of Liangzhou and Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Li Gao, posthumously Prince Wu-Zhao of Liang, died; his heir Li Shiye became governor of Liangzhou and duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 三月，龍驤將軍王鎮惡大破姚泓將姚紹于潼關。

translations.literal: In the third month, General Who Rouses the Dragon Wang Zhen'e inflicted a great defeat on Yao Hong's general Yao Shao at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Wang Zhen'e, general who rouses the dragon, shattered Yao Shao, Yao Hong's general, at Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 夏，劉裕敗魏將鵝青于河曲，斬青裨將阿薄干。

translations.literal: In summer, Liu Yu defeated the Wei general E Qing at a bend of the Yellow River and beheaded Qing's lieutenant Abogan.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Liu Yu routed the Wei commander E Qing in a river bend and slew his subordinate Abogan.

sentences.zh: 是月，涼公李士業大敗沮渠蒙遜于鮮支澗。

translations.literal: That month, Duke of Liang Li Shiye inflicted a great defeat on Juqu Mengxun at Xianzhi Stream.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Li Shiye, duke of Liang, crushed Juqu Mengxun at Xianzhi Stream.

sentences.zh: 五月，劉裕克潼關。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Liu Yu took Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Liu Yu forced Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，會稽王脩之薨。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Prince Xiuzhi of Guiji died.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Sima Xiuzhi, Prince of Guiji, died.

sentences.zh: 六月癸亥，林邑獻馴象、白鸚鵡。

translations.literal: On guihai of the sixth month, Linyi presented tame elephants and white parrots.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai in the sixth month Linyi offered trained elephants and white cockatoos.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，劉裕克長安，執姚泓，收其彝器，歸諸京師。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Liu Yu took Chang'an, captured Yao Hong, seized his ritual bronzes, and sent them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Liu Yu entered Chang'an, took Yao Hong prisoner, confiscated the dynastic tripods, and forwarded them to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 南海賊徐道期陷廣州，始興相劉謙之討平之。

translations.literal: The South Sea bandit Xu Daoqi took Guangzhou; Minister of Shixing Liu Qianzhi campaigned against him and pacified the region.
translations.idiomatic: The pirate Xu Daoqi from the southern sea seized Guangzhou; Liu Qianzhi, minister of Shixing, suppressed him.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月辛未，左僕射、前將軍劉穆之卒。

translations.literal: On xinwei of winter, the eleventh month, Vice Director of the Left, former general Liu Muzhi, died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei in the eleventh month Liu Muzhi, left vice director of the secretariat and former general, died.

sentences.zh: 十四年春正月辛巳，大赦。

translations.literal: On xinsi of the first month of spring in the fourteenth year, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi in the first month of Yixi 14 the court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 青州刺史沈田子害龍驤將軍王鎮惡于長安。

translations.literal: The inspector of Qingzhou, Shen Tianzi, murdered General Who Rouses the Dragon Wang Zhen'e at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tianzi, inspector of Qingzhou, assassinated Wang Zhen'e, general who rouses the dragon, at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 夏六月，劉裕爲相國，進封宋公。

translations.literal: In summer, the sixth month, Liu Yu was made minister of state and advanced in fief to Duke of Song.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Liu Yu became minister of state and was promoted to duke of Song.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，以涼公士業爲鎮西將軍，封酒泉公。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Duke of Liang Shiye was made General Who Garrisons the West and enfeoffed as Duke of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Li Shiye, duke of Liang, was named general who garrisons the west and invested duke of Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 十一月，赫連勃勃大敗王師于青泥北。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Helian Bobo inflicted a great defeat on the imperial army north of Qingni.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Helian Bobo routed government troops north of Qingni.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史朱齡石焚長安宮殿，奔于潼關。

translations.literal: The inspector of Yongzhou, Zhu Lingshi, burned the palaces and halls of Chang'an and fled to Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Lingshi, inspector of Yongzhou, set fire to the Chang'an palaces and bolted to Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 尋又大潰，齡石死之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward came another great rout, and Lingshi died in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the army collapsed again, and Zhu Lingshi perished in the disaster.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊寅，帝崩于東堂，時年三十七。

translations.literal: On wuyin of the twelfth month, the emperor died in the East Hall, aged thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin in the twelfth month the emperor expired in the East Hall at the age of thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 葬休平陵。

translations.literal: He was buried at Xiuping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: They laid him to rest at Xiuping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 帝不惠，自少及長，口不能言，雖寒暑之變，無以辯也。

translations.literal: The emperor was not quick of wit; from youth to adulthood he could not speak, and could not even tell cold from heat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was mentally impaired: from boyhood he never learned to speak and could not distinguish warmth from cold.

sentences.zh: 凡所動止，皆非己出。

translations.literal: Every motion and rest was decided by others, not himself.
translations.idiomatic: Every move he made was dictated for him; he issued no orders of his own.

sentences.zh: 故桓玄之纂，因此獲全。

translations.literal: Therefore when Huan Xuan usurped the throne, he survived on that account.
translations.idiomatic: That was how he survived Huan Xuan's usurpation unscathed.

sentences.zh: 初讖云「昌明之後有二帝」，劉裕將爲禪代，故密使王韶之縊帝而立恭帝，以應二帝云。

translations.literal: At first a prophecy had said, “After Changming there will be two emperors”; as Liu Yu was about to force abdication, he secretly sent Wang Shaozhi to strangle the emperor and set up the Emperor Gong, thereby fulfilling the “two emperors” saying.
translations.idiomatic: A prophecy had long read, “After Changming come two emperors”; when Liu Yu prepared to seize the throne, he secretly ordered Wang Shaozhi to throttle the sovereign and install Emperor Gong, matching the omen of two reigns.

sentences.zh: 義熙五年，置左右長史、司馬、從事中郎四人，加羽葆鼓吹。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yixi, four posts of senior and junior chief clerk, marshal, and retainer secretary were established, with feather-canopy escort and drum music added.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi 5 the court added four adjutant posts—left and right senior and junior clerks, marshals, and secretaries—with feathered canopy and martial music for the prince's train.

sentences.zh: 十二年，詔曰：「大司馬明德懋親，大尉道勳光大，並徽序彝倫，燮和二氣，髦俊引領，思佐鼎飪。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, an edict said: "The Grand Marshal's bright virtue exalts kin; the Grand Commandant's way and merit illumine the age; both set in good order the constant norms and harmonize the two qi, while outstanding men crane their necks, longing to help season the cauldron of state.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi 12 a rescript declared: "The grand marshal's luminous virtue honors the blood royal; the grand commandant's achievement magnifies the Way; together they array the moral order and tune yin and yang, and every brilliant talent strains to join in refining the great stew.

sentences.zh: 而雅尚沖挹，四門弗辟，誠合大雅謙虛之道，實違急賢贊世之務。

translations.literal: Yet they cultivate lofty withdrawal and have not opened their gates to recruits—this indeed matches the great pattern of modesty, yet it runs counter to the urgent task of aiding the age with worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they cling to lofty reserve and keep their gates closed to nominees—noble humility, to be sure, but it frustrates the pressing need to enlist sages for the realm."

sentences.zh: 昔蒲輪載徵，異人並出，東平開府，奇士向臻，濟濟之盛，朕有欽焉。

translations.literal: In old days the rush-wheeled carriage summoned the extraordinary, and they came forth together; the Prince of Dongping opened his mansion, and rare talents thronged in; such teeming excellence fills Us with admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Once the cushioned cart summoned men of genius until they crowded the capital; when the Prince of Dongping opened his headquarters, strange worthies flocked in—such flourishing excellence moves Our deepest respect."

sentences.zh: 可敕二府，依舊辟召，必將明敭俊乂，嗣軌前賢矣。

translations.literal: Let the two offices be ordered, according to precedent, to open recruitment; they will surely raise up splendid talent and tread in the tracks of former worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Charge both administrations to resume normal appointment of staff, that they may lift up the excellent and follow the example of past sages."

sentences.zh: 」於是始辟召掾屬。

translations.literal: Thereupon they began to summon clerks and subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Recruitment of aides to the two bureaus began from that day.

sentences.zh: 時太尉裕都督中外諸軍，詔曰：「大司馬地隆任重，親賢莫貳。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Commandant Yu was area commander over all military affairs inside and outside; an edict said: "The Grand Marshal's station is exalted and his burden heavy; among kin and worthies he has no peer.
translations.idiomatic: While Liu Yu as grand commandant commanded every army, the throne proclaimed: "The grand marshal's rank is lofty and his charge weighty; among kinsmen and worthies he stands without rival."

sentences.zh: 雖府受節度，可身無致敬。」

translations.literal: Although his administration falls under staff direction, in person he need not perform acts of deference."
translations.idiomatic: Though his office answers to your staff orders, you may omit in person the ritual bows otherwise due."

sentences.zh: 劉裕之北征也，帝上疏，請帥所莅，啓行戎路，修敬山陵。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu marched north, the emperor submitted a memorial asking to lead the region under his charge, to set out on the war road, and to pay reverence at the mausolea.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu went north the emperor memorialized, asking to take command of his own jurisdiction, join the campaign route, and sweep the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 朝廷從之，乃與裕俱發。

translations.literal: The court approved, and he therefore set out together with Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The court assented, and the sovereign traveled with Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 及有司以卽戎不得奉辭陵廟，帝復上疏曰：「臣推轂閫外，將革寒暑，不獲展情埏璲私心罔極。

translations.literal: When the authorities ruled that, being under arms, he could not pay respects at the ancestral shrines, the emperor again memorialized, saying: "Your subject pushes the chariot outside the gates and will pass through heat and cold; I cannot unfold my heart upon the sacred mounds—my private grief knows no bound."
translations.idiomatic: When officials said martial law barred visits to the temples, the emperor wrote again: "Your servant drives the war chariot beyond the passes and will endure summer and winter; barred from the tombs, my heart finds no rest."

sentences.zh: 伏願天慈，特垂聽許，使臣微誠粗申，卽路無恨。

translations.literal: We humbly pray Heaven's compassion will especially grant consent, so that your subject's humble sincerity may find some expression, and I may set out without regret.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Heaven's mercy to grant a special hearing, that this humble devotion may find partial voice and I may take the road without regret.

sentences.zh: 」許之。

translations.literal: Permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted his plea.

sentences.zh: 及姚泓滅，歸于京都。

translations.literal: When Yao Hong was destroyed, he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Yao Hong fell, the emperor returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十四年十二月戊寅，安帝崩。

translations.literal: On wuyin of the twelfth month of the fourteenth year, Emperor An died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin in the twelfth month of Yixi 14 Emperor An died.

sentences.zh: 劉裕矯稱遺詔曰：「唯我有晉，誕膺明命，業隆九有，光宅四海。

translations.literal: Liu Yu falsely announced a testamentary edict saying: "We alone have received the bright mandate of Jin; our enterprise towers over the nine provinces and our light fills the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu forged a dying rescript: "Our house of Jin alone has received the luminous charge; its work rises over the nine domains and its glory floods the four seas."

sentences.zh: 朕以不德，屬當多難，幸賴宰輔，拯厥顛覆。

translations.literal: We, of little virtue, have faced many hardships, yet have relied on the ministers to save us from overturn.
translations.idiomatic: We, lacking in virtue, met repeated calamities, yet leaned on the chief ministers to lift us from ruin."

sentences.zh: 仍恃保祐，克黜禍亂，遂冕旒辰極，混一六合。

translations.literal: Still trusting in their protection, we were able to cast out disaster and disorder, then to don the crown at the pole star and unite the six directions.
translations.idiomatic: Still trusting their guardianship, we drove off plague and rebellion, mounted the throne at the zenith, and brought the six quarters under one rule."

sentences.zh: 方憑阿衡，惟新洪業，而遘疾大漸，將遂弗興。

translations.literal: We had hoped to lean on the Yi Yin of the age and renew the great enterprise, but a grave illness worsens and We shall not rise again.
translations.idiomatic: We looked to lean on an Yi Yin for this age and renew the grand task, yet grave illness deepens and We shall not recover."

sentences.zh: 仰惟祖宗靈命。

translations.literal: We look up to the numinous charge of the ancestors."
translations.idiomatic: We lift Our eyes to the spirit-mandate of the ancestral kings."

sentences.zh: 親賢是荷。

translations.literal: The burden falls on the worthy kin."
translations.idiomatic: The charge rests with the worthy among Our kin."

sentences.zh: 咨爾大司馬、琅邪王，體自先皇，明德光懋，屬惟儲貳，衆望攸集。

translations.literal: We charge you, Grand Marshal, Prince of Langye, born of the former emperor, of bright virtue and glorious merit, the rightful heir apparent in whom all expectation gathers.
translations.idiomatic: We hereby name you, grand marshal, Prince of Langye, sprung from the late emperor, of shining virtue and towering merit, the destined heir on whom every hope converges."

sentences.zh: 其君臨晉邦，奉係宗祀，允執其中，燮和天下。

translations.literal: Rule the domain of Jin, uphold the ancestral sacrifices, hold fast the mean, and harmonize all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Rule the state of Jin, maintain the temple offerings, keep to the central way, and bring harmony to the realm."

sentences.zh: 闡揚末誥，無廢我高祖之景命。

translations.literal: Proclaim Our final commands; do not abandon the splendid mandate of Our high ancestor."
translations.idiomatic: Publish these last instructions; do not cast away the bright mandate of Our founding forebear."

sentences.zh: 」是日，卽帝位，大赦。

translations.literal: That same day he assumed the imperial throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he ascended the throne and ordered a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 元熙元年春正月壬辰朔，改元。

translations.literal: On renchen, the first day of the first month of spring in the first year of Yuanxi, the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: Spring, first month of Yuanxi 1, new moon on renchen: the reign title was changed to Yuanxi.

sentences.zh: 以山陵未厝，不朝會。

translations.literal: Because the imperial tombs were not yet settled, court assemblies were suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Court audiences were suspended while the late sovereign's tomb remained unfinished.

sentences.zh: 立皇后褚氏。

translations.literal: Empress Lady Chu was established.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chu was enthroned as empress.

sentences.zh: 甲午，徵劉裕還朝。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Liu Yu was summoned back to court.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Liu Yu was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，有星孛于太微西籓。

translations.literal: On wuxu, a star appeared broom-like at the western barrier of the Supreme Palace enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu a comet blazed along the western fence of the Supreme Palace constellation.

sentences.zh: 庚申，葬安皇帝于休平陵。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Emperor An was buried at Xiuping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Emperor An was interred at Xiuping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 帝受朝，懸而不樂。

translations.literal: The emperor held court, bells hung in silence and no music played.
translations.idiomatic: The new emperor held audience with the bells stilled and the orchestra silent.

sentences.zh: 以驃騎將軍劉道憐爲司空。

translations.literal: General of Agile Cavalry Liu Daolian was made minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daolian, general of agile cavalry, was appointed minister of works.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，劉裕移鎮壽陽。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, Liu Yu moved his headquarters to Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Liu Yu shifted his base to Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 以劉懷慎爲前將軍、北徐州刺史，鎮彭城。

translations.literal: Liu Huaishen was made former general and inspector of northern Xuzhou, garrisoning Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huaishen became former general and inspector of northern Xuzhou, with headquarters at Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 九月，劉裕自解揚州。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Liu Yu resigned the inspectorate of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Liu Yu relinquished the governorship of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 冬十月乙酉，裕以其子桂陽公義真爲揚州刺史。

translations.literal: On yiyou of winter, the tenth month, Yu made his son, Duke Yizhen of Guiyang, inspector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou in the tenth month Liu Yu named his son Liu Yizhen, duke of Guiyang, inspector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 十一月丁亥朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: On dinghai, the first day of the eleventh month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: New moon on dinghai in the eleventh month: the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 十二月辛卯，裕加殊禮。

translations.literal: On xinmao of the twelfth month, Yu was granted extraordinary honors.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao in the twelfth month Liu Yu received exceptional ceremonial privileges.

sentences.zh: 己卯，太史奏，黑龍四見于東方。

translations.literal: On jimao, the grand astrologer reported that black dragons had appeared four times in the east.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao the director of astronomy reported four sightings of black dragons in the eastern sky.

sentences.zh: 二年夏六月壬戌，劉裕至于京師。

translations.literal: On renxu of summer, the sixth month of the second year, Liu Yu reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu in the sixth month of Yuanxi 2 Liu Yu arrived at the capital.

sentences.zh: 傅亮承裕密旨，諷帝禪位，草詔，請帝書之。

translations.literal: Fu Liang, acting on Liu Yu's secret instructions, hinted that the emperor should abdicate, drafted the edict, and asked the emperor to copy it in his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Liang, carrying Liu Yu's private orders, urged abdication, composed the text, and bade the emperor trace it in his own brush.

sentences.zh: 帝欣然謂左右曰：「晉氏久已失之，今復何恨。

translations.literal: The emperor said cheerfully to those beside him: “The house of Jin lost the realm long ago; what regret is there now.”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned happily to his attendants and said, “The Jin mandate slipped away ages ago; I feel no bitterness now.”

sentences.zh: 」乃書赤紙爲詔。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wrote the edict on red paper.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon brushed the abdication rescript on red paper.

sentences.zh: 甲子，遂遜于琅邪第。

translations.literal: On jiazi, he then yielded the throne at the Langye princely mansion.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi he abdicated at the Langye princely residence.

sentences.zh: 劉裕以帝爲零陵王，居于秣陵，行晉正朔，車旗服色一如其舊，有其文而不備其禮。

translations.literal: Liu Yu made the emperor Prince of Lingling, dwelling at Moling, observing Jin's calendar and regalia as of old, with the forms of state preserved in writing but not fully in ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu demoted him to prince of Lingling, quartered him at Moling, let him keep the Jin calendar and insignia as before, granting him the titles on paper while withholding full court ceremony.

sentences.zh: 帝自是之後，深慮禍機，褚後常在帝側，飲食所資，皆出褚后，故宋人莫得伺其隟，宋永初二年九月丁丑，裕使後兄叔度請后；

translations.literal: After this the emperor lived in deep fear of deadly plots; Empress Chu constantly remained at his side, and all provisions for drink and food came from the empress, so that the men of Liu Song could find no opening; on dingchou in the ninth month of the second year of Yongchu of Liu Song, Yu sent the empress's elder brother Shudu to summon the empress away;
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the sovereign lived in dread of assassination; Empress Chu never left his side, tasting and supplying every meal so Liu Yu's agents found no chink—until dingchou in the ninth month of Yongchu 2, when Liu Yu sent her brother Chu Shudu to lure her from the chamber;

sentences.zh: 有間，兵人逾垣而入，弑帝于內房。

translations.literal: After a short interval, armed men climbed the wall and entered, assassinating the emperor in his inner chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later soldiers scaled the wall, broke in, and slew him in his private rooms.

sentences.zh: 時年三十六。

translations.literal: At the time he was thirty-six sui old.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty-six years of age.

sentences.zh: 諡恭皇帝，葬沖平陵。

translations.literal: He was given the posthumous title Emperor Gong and buried at Chongping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: They canonized him as Emperor Gong and laid him to rest at Chongping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 帝幼時性頗忍急，及在籓國，曾令善射者射馬爲戲。

translations.literal: In childhood the emperor's nature was rather cruel and impatient; when he held a princely fief, he once ordered skilled archers to shoot horses for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was harsh and hasty; after receiving his princely domain he once made expert bowmen use live horses for target practice.

sentences.zh: 旣而有人云：「馬者國姓，而自殺之，不祥之甚。

translations.literal: Someone then said: "The horse is the dynastic surname; for you yourself to kill it is supremely inauspicious."
translations.idiomatic: A courtier warned him: "Horse matches the imperial name; shooting it yourself is the worst of omens."

sentences.zh: 」帝亦悟，甚悔之。

translations.literal: The emperor understood as well and deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: The prince took the point and bitterly regretted the sport.

sentences.zh: 其後復深信浮屠道，鑄貨千萬，造丈六金像，親于瓦官寺迎之，步從十許里。

translations.literal: Later he came to put deep faith in Buddhism, casting cash to the value of ten million, commissioning a sixteen-foot metal image, and personally welcoming it at Waguan Monastery, walking in attendance for more than ten li.
translations.idiomatic: He later embraced Buddhism fervently, spending millions in coin on a sixteen-foot gilt statue, which he met in person at Waguan Monastery and escorted on foot for ten li or more.

sentences.zh: 安帝旣不惠，帝每侍左右，消息溫涼寢食之節，以恭謹聞，時人稱焉。

translations.literal: Since Emperor An was not quick of wit, the emperor constantly attended him at his side, regulating every turn of warmth, coolness, sleep, and meals, and became known for humble reverence; people of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Emperor An could not care for himself, the prince waited on him without fail, tending every comfort of heat, cold, food, and sleep, and earned a name for dutiful devotion that contemporaries admired.

sentences.zh: 始，元帝以丁丑歲稱晉王，置宗廟，使郭璞筮之，云「享二百年。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Emperor Yuan assumed the title Prince of Jin in the dingchou year, he established the ancestral temple and had Guo Pu cast milfoil; the response said, "You shall enjoy two hundred years."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan first took the title Prince of Jin in the dingchou year, he founded the dynastic shrine and asked Guo Pu to divine by milfoil; the oracle read that the house would endure two hundred years.

sentences.zh: 」自丁丑至禪代之歲，年在庚申，爲一百四歲。

translations.literal: From dingchou to the year of abdication fell gengshen, which makes one hundred four sui.
translations.idiomatic: From dingchou down to the abdication year gengshen is only one hundred four years by the count.

sentences.zh: 然丁丑始係西晉，庚申終入宋年，所餘惟一百有二歲耳。

translations.literal: Yet dingchou marked only the start of Western Jin's reckoning, while gengshen fell already in Song years; what remained was only one hundred two sui.
translations.idiomatic: Yet dingchou marks only Western Jin's start, while gengshen falls under Song—so the true span is just one hundred two years.

sentences.zh: 璞蓋以百二之期促，故婉而倒之爲二百也。

translations.literal: Guo Pu must have thought the term of one hundred two too short, and therefore tactfully inverted the figures to read two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu, seeing how brief one hundred two years would sound, softened the blow by reversing the digits to two hundred.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：安帝卽位之辰，鐘無妄之日，道子、元顯並傾朝政，主昏臣亂，未有如斯不亡者也。

translations.literal: The historiographers say: When Emperor An ascended the throne, it was the day of the hexagram "No Error," yet Daozi and Yuanxian together capsized court governance; never was there a ruler so benighted and ministers so chaotic without the dynasty's perishing.
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: Emperor An came to the throne on an auspicious day, yet Sima Daozi and Sima Yuanxian wrecked the government together—never was a court so blinded by its prince and so ruined by its ministers without paying the price of extinction.

sentences.zh: 雖有手握戎麾，心存舊國，迴首無良，忽焉蕭散。

translations.literal: Although some still grasped the commander's banner and harbored the old state in their hearts, they looked behind them and found no good allies, and in a trice scattered like wind-strewn reeds.
translations.idiomatic: Some still held batons of war and longed for the former dynasty, yet they turned and saw no worthy support, and in a breath thinned away like chaff on the wind.

sentences.zh: 於是桓玄乘釁，勢逾飆指，六師咸泯，隻馬徂遷。

translations.literal: Thereupon Huan Xuan seized the opening; his momentum swifter than a whirlwind's finger—the six hosts were all annihilated, and the imperial carriage fled with scarcely a retinue.
translations.idiomatic: Then Huan Xuan exploited the breach; his surge outran the whirlwind—the loyalist hosts vanished, and the court fled on a handful of horses.

sentences.zh: 是以宋高非典午之臣，孫恩豈金行之寇。

translations.literal: Thus the founding lord of Song was no loyal minister of the house of Sima, nor was Sun En merely a bandit against the Jin of the metal phase.
translations.idiomatic: So Liu Yu was never a true servant of the Sima line, and Sun En was never simply a spoiler of the metal-phase Jin—both were forces that unmade the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 若乃世遇顛覆，則恭皇斯甚。

translations.literal: If one speaks of generations that met utter overturn, none matches the fate of Emperor Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Among reigns that knew total collapse, none was graver than that of Emperor Gong.

sentences.zh: 於越之民，詎熏丹穴，會稽之侶，寧歎入臣。

translations.literal: The folk of Yuyue were not driven to smoke out mountain cinnabar fastnesses; the company of Kuaiji had little cause to sigh at entering another's service.
translations.idiomatic: The southeast did not rise to scorched-earth extremes; the Kuaiji elite were spared the worst shame of forced submission—yet the throne fell all the same.

sentences.zh: 去皇屋而歸來，灑丹書而不恨。

translations.literal: They might quit the imperial roof yet walk away alive; they might face vermilion writs of sentence yet harbor no lasting rancor.
translations.idiomatic: Some could leave the palace and still draw breath; some could read their death warrant in red ink yet feel little lasting spite—such was the strange mercy and cruelty of the hour.

sentences.zh: 夫五運攸革，三微數盡，猶高秋彫候，理之自然。

translations.literal: When the five circuits of fortune turn and the reckoning of the three micro-ages is exhausted, it is like the withering season of deep autumn—the pattern of nature.
translations.idiomatic: When the five phases revolve and the three micro-calendars run out, it is as in late autumn when the frost takes the leaves—inevitable law.

sentences.zh: 觀其搖落，人有爲之流漣者也。

translations.literal: Gazing on that fall, there were men who shed tears for it.
translations.idiomatic: To watch that shedding still moves a reader to sorrow.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：安承流湎，大盜斯張。

translations.literal: Encomium: An inherited throne drowned in wine; then the great robber spread his nets wide.
translations.idiomatic: The verdict runs: An took a legacy awash in drink, and the arch-thief spread his snare.

sentences.zh: 恭乃寓命，他人是綱。

translations.literal: Gong merely lodged his borrowed life; another hand held the reins.
translations.idiomatic: Gong was a guest on the throne; another pulled every rope.

sentences.zh: 猶存周赧，始立懷王。

translations.literal: Like King Nan of Zhou still enthroned, like Emperor Huai of Chu first set up—titles without substance.
translations.idiomatic: He resembled King Nan of late Zhou, or Emperor Huai of Chu—raised up in name alone.

sentences.zh: 虛尊假號，異術同亡。

translations.literal: Empty veneration and sham titles—strange contrivance, yet the same road to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Hollow honor and borrowed style—odd pageantry, but the same annihilation in the end.
